title: RTCP: Handle non-null terminated SDES in compound packet
description:
RFC 3550 Section 6.5 is clear that "The list of items in each chunk
MUST be terminated by one or more null octets, the first of which is
interpreted as an item type of zero to denote the end of the list."

Despite this, we have a long-standing check for the end of the frame
because a number of implementations do not include the null bytes.
This can be handled because the RTCP packet has a length, and so
message processing can simply stop at the end of the packet.

As currently implemented, this only works when the SDES is a sole
RTCP packet or the final RTCP packet in a compound frame, because the
tvbuffer is not truncated. The RTCP header has a length value contained
with in, and so truncating the tvbuffer passed into SDES makes this
check work for compound frames as well.

Add an expert info warning when dissection of a list of items stops due
to reaching the end of the message instead of a null terminator.
